learningGoals: Identify and name different parts of a bicycle like the wheels, seat, pedal, and bell. 🔔
Recognize and read simple action words related to movement, such as riding, pushing, and pulling. 🏃‍♂️
Describe the colors of different bicycles using English color names. 🔴
Read simple, short sentences aloud with confidence and a clear voice. 📖
Express the joy of outdoor play and share their feelings about riding a bicycle. 🌳
conversationStarters: If you could have a magical bicycle, what color would it be and where would you ride it? ✨
Can you show me how you ring a bicycle bell and make the sound? 🎶
How does your body feel when you run or ride a bicycle outside? 😊
teachingTips: Point to parts of a real bicycle or a picture and ask your child to name them aloud in English. 🚲
Encourage your child to act out action words like 'push', 'pull', and 'ride' while saying the words out loud. 🏃‍♀️
Make a fun game out of spotting colorful bicycles or vehicles when you go for a walk together. 🚶‍♂️
Read the chapter aloud together, taking turns to read one sentence at a time to build their reading confidence. 📚
Practice phonics by emphasizing the starting sounds of new words, like the 'b' sound for bicycle and bell. 🗣️

funActivities.title: Draw Your Dream Bicycle 🖍️
funActivities.description: Ask your child to draw and color their dream bicycle on a piece of paper. Help them write labels for the different parts like the seat, wheels, and bell in English.

funActivities.title: Bicycle Action 'Simon Says' 🧍‍♂️
funActivities.description: Play a quick game of Simon Says using chapter action words. Say 'Simon says pretend to pedal' or 'Simon says ring the bell' to combine physical movement with vocabulary.

funActivities.title: Outdoor Wheel Hunt 🔍
funActivities.description: Take a short walk outside and ask your child to spot things with wheels or things they can push and pull. Encourage them to name these objects in English.
